page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.DenseIO.A4.Ax.72 is a bare metal compute instance within the Dense I/O family designed for I/O-intensive and data-heavy enterprise workloads. It is powered by the arm64 Ampere AmpereOne-M platform, providing 144 physical cores and 144 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core to prevent resource contention. The server integrates 1152 GB of physical memory, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core allocation.

A central component of this bare metal configuration is its bundled local storage array, offering 27,200 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Because this is a bare metal deployment, operations bypass hypervisor translation layers, enabling direct physical access to the high-capacity NVMe drives. No discrete GPUs are provisioned on this instance type, and the machine includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address for networking connectivity.

From an efficiency perspective, the high core density of the AmpereOne-M processor paired with extensive local NVMe storage reduces reliance on external network-attached storage volumes for data-intensive processing. Workloads must support the arm64 instruction set architecture, as x86 vector or virtualization extensions are not available. This architecture is appropriate for high-throughput transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, big data analytics engines, and large-scale data ingestion pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.DenseIO.A4.Ax.72 is a bare metal server from the Dense I/O family engineered for large-scale data storage and low-latency processing. It features 144 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 Ampere AmpereOne-M platform, running one thread per core without hyperthreading overhead. The hardware configuration includes 1152 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and is bundled with 27,200 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking GPU acceleration, the server focuses hardware resources on processing throughput and direct disk I/O. The extensive on-host solid-state capacity eliminates the latency and overhead of network-attached block devices, making it cost-efficient for heavy data footprints. BM.DenseIO.A4.Ax.72 is well-suited for high-concurrency databases, distributed datastores, big data analytics, and real-time transaction processing systems optimized for ARM architectures.
